claim: The CRISPR-Cas9 targeted nuclease technology allows the insertion of genetic modifications with single base-pair precision.
source: The CRISPR-Cas9 targeted nuclease technology allows the insertion of genetic modifications with single base-pair precision.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about CRISPR-Cas9 capabilities.

claim: Mammalian cells preferentially repair Cas9-induced DNA double-strand breaks via error-prone end-joining pathways rather than via homology-directed repair mechanisms.
source: The preference of mammalian cells to repair Cas9-induced DNA double-strand breaks via error-prone end-joining pathways rather than via homology-directed repair mechanisms, however, leads to relatively low rates of precise editing from donor DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA repair pathway preferences in mammalian cells.

claim: Covalent linkage of the donor template to Cas9 increases correction rates up to 24-fold.
source: Here we show that spatial and temporal co-localization of the donor template and Cas9 via covalent linkage increases the correction rates up to 24-fold
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The enhancement in correction rates from covalent linkage is mainly caused by an increase of donor template concentration in the nucleus.
source: demonstrate that the effect is mainly caused by an increase of donor template concentration in the nucleus
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from experimental data in the study.

claim: Enhanced correction rates were observed in multiple cell types.
source: Enhanced correction rates were observed in multiple cell types and on different genomic loci
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from different cell types tested in the study.

claim: Enhanced correction rates were observed on different genomic loci.
source: Enhanced correction rates were observed in multiple cell types and on different genomic loci
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from different genomic targets tested in the study.

claim: Covalently linking the donor template to the Cas9 complex provides advantages for clinical applications where high-fidelity repair is desired.
source: suggesting that covalently linking the donor template to the Cas9 complex provides advantages for clinical applications where high-fidelity repair is desired.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: A programmable chimeric single guide RNA (sgRNA) directs the Cas9 nuclease to the genomic region of interest.
source: In its most widespread variant a programmable chimeric single guide RNA (sgRNA) directs the Cas9 nuclease to the genomic region of interest, where it generates a site-specific DNA double-strand break (DSB) (Mali et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CRISPR-Cas9 mechanism, supported by citation.

claim: Cas9 generates a site-specific DNA double-strand break (DSB) at the genomic region of interest.
source: In its most widespread variant a programmable chimeric single guide RNA (sgRNA) directs the Cas9 nuclease to the genomic region of interest, where it generates a site-specific DNA double-strand break (DSB) (Mali et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CRISPR-Cas9 mechanism, supported by citation.

claim: In mammalian cells, repair of DSBs by different end-joining pathways often leads to the formation of insertions or deletions (indels).
source: In mammalian cells the repair of DSBs by different end-joining (EJ) pathways, such as classical non-homologous end joining (c-NHEJ), alternative non-homologous end-joining (a-NHEJ), or single-strand annealing (SSA) often leads to the formation of insertions or deletions (indels) (Shalem et al., 2014; Ceccaldi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA repair outcomes, supported by citations.

claim: Mammalian cells can resolve DSBs via homology-directed repair (HDR) mechanisms when a donor template is provided.
source: Alternatively, when a donor template is provided, mammalian cells can also resolve DSBs via homology-directed repair (HDR) mechanisms, such as the classical homologous recombination (HR) pathway (Mao et al., 2008) and the Fanconi Anemia (FA) repair pathway (Richardson, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA repair mechanisms, supported by citations.

claim: Repair from an ectopic donor oligonucleotide via HDR mechanisms enables the introduction of DNA modifications with single base pair precision.
source: While the formation of indels allows the elimination of gene function, repair from an ectopic donor oliogonucleotide (oligo) via HDR mechanisms enables the introduction of DNA modifications with single base pair precision (van den Bosch et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HDR capabilities, supported by citation.

claim: Therapeutic applications of CRISPR-Cas9 generally require the precise correction of pathogenic mutations using donor templates.
source: Therapeutic applications of CRISPR-Cas9 generally require the precise correction of pathogenic mutations using donor templates.
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for therapeutic applications based on established knowledge.

claim: DSBs introduced in mammalian cells are predominantly repaired by error-prone EJ pathways.
source: However, DSBs introduced in mammalian cells are predominantly repaired by error-prone EJ pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA repair pathway preferences in mammalian cells.

claim: Error-prone repair indirectly competes with HDR by preventing CRISPR-Cas9 complex retargeting.
source: As the resulting indels inhibit the CRISPR-Cas9 complex from retargeting the locus, error-prone repair indirectly competes with HDR, and therefore reduces the rates of precise correction from donor templates.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism by which error-prone repair affects HDR rates.

claim: If the targeted allele is a hypomorph with residual gene function, the generated indels can further worsen the clinical phenotype of the disease.
source: Furthermore, if the targeted allele is a hypomorph with residual gene function, the generated indels can further worsen the clinical phenotype of the disease (Chu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about potential negative consequences, supported by citation.

claim: HDR pathways are primarily active during the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle.
source: Based on the knowledge that HDR pathways are primarily active during the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, cells have been synchronized prior to CRISPR-Cas9 delivery (Lin et al., 2014a), and Cas9 expression has been limited to the S/G2/M phase of the cell cycle (Gutschner et al., 2016; Howden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell cycle regulation of HDR, supported by citations.

claim: Cells have been synchronized prior to CRISPR-Cas9 delivery to enhance HDR.
source: Based on the knowledge that HDR pathways are primarily active during the S/G2 phase of the cell cycle, cells have been synchronized prior to CRISPR-Cas9 delivery (Lin et al., 2014a)
evidence: This is a statement about previous approaches to enhance HDR, supported by citation.

claim: Cas9 expression has been limited to the S/G2/M phase of the cell cycle to enhance HDR.
source: Cas9 expression has been limited to the S/G2/M phase of the cell cycle (Gutschner et al., 2016; Howden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about previous approaches to enhance HDR, supported by citations.

claim: HDR has been increased by chemically modulating the EJ and HDR pathways.
source: Other studies have increased HDR by chemically modulating the EJ and HDR pathways (Chu et al., 2015; Maruyama et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2015; Song et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a statement about previous approaches to enhance HDR, supported by citations.

claim: HDR has been increased by rationally designing DNA repair templates with optimal homology arm lengths.
source: and by rationally designing DNA repair templates with optimal homology arm lengths (Richardson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about previous approaches to enhance HDR, supported by citation.

claim: The availability of the DNA repair template might present a rate-limiting factor for HDR.
source: In addition, it has been proposed that the availability of the DNA repair template might present a rate-limiting factor for HDR
evidence: This is a hypothesis from previous work, indicated by 'has been proposed'.

claim: Enhancing the local concentration of donor oligos could increase the correction rates.
source: and that enhancing the local concentration of donor oligos could increase the correction rates (Ruff et al., 2014; Carlson-Stevermer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from previous work, supported by citations.

claim: A fluorescent reporter system was generated to measure HDR efficiencies in a rapid and high-throughput manner.
source: To be able to measure HDR efficiencies of novel CRISPR-Cas9 variants in a rapid and high-throughput manner, we first generated a fluorescent reporter system (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the study.

claim: The reporter cassette was stably integrated in HEK293T cells.
source: In brief, the reporter cassette was stably integrated in HEK293T cells
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.

claim: The reporter cassette expresses a green fluorescent protein (GFP) that is preceded by an inactive mutant version of a red fluorescent protein (mutRFP).
source: and expresses a green fluorescent protein (GFP) that is preceded by an inactive mutant version of a red fluorescent protein (mutRFP).
evidence: This is a description of the reporter system design.

claim: Precise correction of the mutation via HDR from donor templates leads to re-activation of RFP activity.
source: While precise correction of the mutation via HDR from donor templates leads to re-activation of RFP activity
evidence: This is a description of how the reporter system functions.

claim: The generation of frame shifts via error-prone EJ pathways leads to loss of GFP activity.
source: the generation of frame shifts via error-prone EJ pathways leads to loss of GFP activity (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: This is a description of how the reporter system functions.

claim: The correction and indel formation events can be visualized by fluorescence imaging and quantified by FACS.
source: The correction and indel formation events can be visualized by fluorescence imaging and quantified by FACS (Figure 2c–d).
evidence: This is a description of the analytical methods used in the study.

claim: Maximal DSB correction rates are reached with ss-donor oligos of approximately 80 bases.
source: In line with previous studies (Zuo et al., 2017), we found that maximal DSB correction rates are reached with ss-donor oligos of approximately 80 bases.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study, consistent with previous work.

claim: The SNAP-tag technology allows covalent binding of O6-benzylguanine (BG)-labeled molecules to SNAP-tag fusion proteins.
source: In order to link the donor oligos to the Cas9 protein, we used the SNAP-tag technology, which allows covalent binding of O6-benzylguanine (BG)-labeled molecules to SNAP-tag fusion proteins (Keppler et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SNAP-tag technology, supported by citation.

claim: Amine-modified oligos were coupled to commercially available amine-reactive BG building blocks to generate O6-benzylguanine (BG)-linked DNA repair templates.
source: To generate O6-benzylguanine (BG)-linked DNA repair templates, we first coupled amine-modified oligos to commercially available amine-reactive BG building blocks (Figure 3a, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the study.

claim: BG-linked oligos were separated from unreacted oligos by HPLC.
source: The BG-linked oligos were further separated from unreacted oligos by HPLC (Figure 3b)
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.

claim: BG-linked oligos were analyzed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to confirm their purity.
source: and analyzed by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) to confirm their purity (Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This is a methodological detail from the study.

claim: Recombinant Cas9 proteins with a SNAP-tag fused to the C-terminus were produced.
source: Next, we produced recombinant Cas9 proteins with a SNAP-tag fused to the C-terminus (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the study.

claim: The fusion proteins were complexed with the BG-coupled oligos.
source: The fusion proteins were then complexed with the BG-coupled oligos
evidence: This is a methodological step described in the study.

claim: Covalent binding of fusion proteins to BG-coupled oligos was confirmed by SDS-PAGE.
source: and covalent binding was confirmed by SDS-PAGE (Figure 3e–h).
evidence: This is experimental validation of the conjugation method.

claim: The protein-oligo conjugate was mixed with in vitro transcribed sgRNAs targeting the mutRFP locus to generate the Cas9 ribonucleoprotein-DNA (RNPD) complex.
source: The protein-oligo conjugate was mixed with in vitro transcribed sgRNAs targeting the mutRFP locus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1g,h), finally generating the Cas9 ribonucleoprotein-DNA (RNPD) complex.
evidence: This is a methodological step described in the study.

claim: The correction efficiency with bound complexes was significantly enhanced from 2.1% to 22.5% with the 65-mers.
source: Notably, the correction efficiency (percentage of corrections in edited cells) with bound complexes was significantly enhanced, from 2.1% to 22.5% with the 65-mers
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: The correction efficiency with bound complexes was significantly enhanced from 8.9% to 25.7% with the 81-mers.
source: and from 8.9% to 25.7% with the 81-mers (Figure 4a, Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: In comparison to unbound complexes, bound complexes represented 11-fold increases with 65-mers.
source: In comparison to unbound complexes this represented 11- and 3-fold increases, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: In comparison to unbound complexes, bound complexes represented 3-fold increases with 81-mers.
source: In comparison to unbound complexes this represented 11- and 3-fold increases, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: A two-component system was developed where the donor oligo is bound to a second catalytically inactive Cas9 complex that binds in close proximity to the DSB.
source: To further test our hypothesis that spatial and temporal co-localization of repair templates and Cas9 enhances correction rates, we next developed an independent approach where the donor oligo is not bound to the Cas9 complex that induces the DSB, but to a second catalytically inactive Cas9 complex that binds in close proximity to the DSB (RNP-RNPD system).
evidence: This is a methodological approach developed in the study.

claim: In the two-component system, the DSB is induced by SpCas9, and the repair template is linked to a catalytically inactive Staphylococcus aureus (Sa)dCas9.
source: To avoid the interchange of sgRNAs between both complexes, we designed a two-component system in which the DSB is induced by SpCas9, and the repair template is linked to a catalytically inactive Staphylococcus aureus (Sa)dCas9 (Figure 4c,d).
evidence: This is a description of the two-component system design.

claim: With the two-component system, the correction efficiency increased from 4.1% to 29.9% with 65-mers.
source: Notably, the correction efficiency increased from 4.1% to 29.9% with 65-mers
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: With the two-component system, the correction efficiency increased from 11.6% to 32.3% with 81-mers.
source: and from 11.6% to 32.3% with 81-mers (Figure 4e, Figure 4—figure supplement 1c,d)
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: At 5-fold lower transfection concentrations, the RNPD system yielded 20-fold increases in repair efficiency with 65-mer repair template oligos compared to the uncoupled RNP complex.
source: Compared to the uncoupled RNP complex, the RNPD system yielded 20-fold and a 4-fold increases in repair efficiency with 65-mer and 81-mer repair template oligos, respectively (Figure 4f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e,f).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: At 5-fold lower transfection concentrations, the RNPD system yielded 4-fold increases in repair efficiency with 81-mer repair template oligos compared to the uncoupled RNP complex.
source: Compared to the uncoupled RNP complex, the RNPD system yielded 20-fold and a 4-fold increases in repair efficiency with 65-mer and 81-mer repair template oligos, respectively (Figure 4f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e,f).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: At 5-fold lower transfection concentrations, the two-component RNP-RNPD system led to a 21-fold increase with 65-mers.
source: Similarly, the two-component RNP-RNPD system led to a 21-fold increase with 65-mers and a 6-fold increase with 81-mers (Figure 4f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e,f).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: At 5-fold lower transfection concentrations, the two-component RNP-RNPD system led to a 6-fold increase with 81-mers.
source: Similarly, the two-component RNP-RNPD system led to a 21-fold increase with 65-mers and a 6-fold increase with 81-mers (Figure 4f, Figure 4—figure supplement 1e,f).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the study.

claim: Linking the repair template to the Cas9 complex leads to improved correction efficiency compared to the unlinked control CRISPR-Cas9 system.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that linking the repair template to the Cas9 complex leads to improved correction efficiency compared to the unlinked control CRISPR-Cas9 system
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The effect of linking the repair template to Cas9 is more pronounced when CRISPR-Cas9 components are delivered at lower concentrations.
source: and that this effect is even more pronounced when CRISPR-Cas9 components are delivered at lower concentrations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: BG-labelling of the donor oligo itself influences the correction efficiencies.
source: We first assessed if the BG-labelling of the donor oligo itself already influences the correction efficiencies, and compared the correction rates of wild-type SpCas9 lacking the SNAP-tag together with either unlabelled oligo or BG-labelled oligo. While the correction rates were enhanced when the donor oligo was labelled with BG, the increase was several fold lower compared to the system where the oligo was conjugated to the Cas9 RNP complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a–c).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: The increase in correction efficiency from BG-labelling alone was several fold lower compared to the system where the oligo was conjugated to the Cas9 RNP complex.
source: While the correction rates were enhanced when the donor oligo was labelled with BG, the increase was several fold lower compared to the system where the oligo was conjugated to the Cas9 RNP complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a–c).
evidence: This is a comparative experimental finding from the study.

claim: Adding the sgRNA to direct SadCas9 in close proximity to the DSB did not further enhance correction rates beyond directing it to the nucleoplasm.
source: Importantly, our results demonstrated that adding the sgRNA did not further enhance correction rates, suggesting that the increase of donor oligo concentration in the nucleoplasm was sufficient to fully account for the positive effect of the Cas9-donor oligo conjugation (Figure 4g, Figure 4—figure supplement 2d,e).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: The increase of donor oligo concentration in the nucleoplasm was sufficient to fully account for the positive effect of the Cas9-donor oligo conjugation.
source: Importantly, our results demonstrated that adding the sgRNA did not further enhance correction rates, suggesting that the increase of donor oligo concentration in the nucleoplasm was sufficient to fully account for the positive effect of the Cas9-donor oligo conjugation (Figure 4g, Figure 4—figure supplement 2d,e).
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Exogenous DNA transport into the nucleus is one of the major barriers to effective gene delivery.
source: In line with these observations, a number of previous studies demonstrated that exogenous DNA transport into the nucleus is one of the major barriers to effective gene delivery (Subramanian et al., 1999; Zanta et al., 1999; Ludtke et al., 1999; Aronsohn and Hughes, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: At the human beta globin (HBB) locus in the K562 cell line, the mean correction efficiency with the RNPD system was 19.6%.
source: We first targeted the human beta globin (HBB) locus in the K562 cell line, and analyzed correction and editing frequencies using next generation sequencing (NGS). The mean correction efficiency with the RNPD system was 19.6%
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the HBB locus in K562 cells, the RNPD system represented a 17-fold increase compared to the control RNP system.
source: The mean correction efficiency with the RNPD system was 19.6%, which represented a 17-fold increase compared to the control RNP system (Figure 5a, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: At the Rosa26 locus in mouse embryonic stem cells, the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was 18.6%.
source: Next we targeted the Rosa26 and proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (Pcsk9) locus in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). Again, the mean correction efficiencies of RNPD systems were significantly increased, to 18.6% at the Rosa26 locus
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the Pcsk9 locus in mouse embryonic stem cells, the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was 23.2%.
source: and 23.2% at the Pcsk9 locus (Figure 5b,c, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the Rosa26 locus in mESCs, the RNPD system represented a 2-fold increase compared to the uncoupled RNP complexes.
source: In comparison to the uncoupled RNP complexes, this represented 2- and 6-fold increases, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: At the Pcsk9 locus in mESCs, the RNPD system represented a 6-fold increase compared to the uncoupled RNP complexes.
source: In comparison to the uncoupled RNP complexes, this represented 2- and 6-fold increases, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: At the reporter locus, the mean percentage of corrected loci increased from 0.8% with the classical Cas9 system to 4.9% with the RNPD system.
source: We found that while the mean percentage of corrected loci increased from 0.8% with the classical Cas9 system to 4.9% with the RNPD system
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the reporter locus, the number of incorrectly edited loci slightly decreased from 12.6% to 9.3% with the RNPD system.
source: the number of incorrectly edited loci slightly decreased from 12.6% to 9.3% (Figure 6a, Supplementary file 2,3,4).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the reporter locus, the RNPD system corresponds to a 7-fold increase in correction efficiency compared to the classical Cas9 system.
source: This corresponds to a 7-fold increase in correction efficiency (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: The analysis of three computationally predicted off-target sites of the reporter locus suggests that the risk for generating off-target mutations is not enhanced with the RNPD system.
source: In addition, the analysis of three computationally predicted off-target sites (Lin et al., 2014b; Cradick et al., 2014) of the reporter locus, suggests that the risk for generating off-target mutations is not enhanced with the RNPD system (Figure 6c, Supplementary file 2,3,4).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the HBB locus in HEK293T cells, the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was 34.4%.
source: In the next step we also targeted and analyzed the endogenous loci HBB, empty spiracles homeobox 1 (EMX1), and C-X-C chemokine receptor type 4 (CXCR4) in HEK293T cells. NGS analysis revealed that in all three loci the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was markedly increased to: 34,4% at the HBB locus
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the EMX1 locus in HEK293T cells, the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was 28.6%.
source: 28.6% at the EMX1 locus
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the CXCR4 locus in HEK293T cells, the mean correction efficiency of the RNPD system was 33.1%.
source: and 33.1% at the CXCR4 locus (Figure 6d,e,f, Supplementary file 2,3,4).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the study.

claim: At the HBB locus in HEK293T cells, the RNPD system represents a 20-fold increase compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system.
source: Compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system this represents a 20-fold, a 10-fold, and a 24-fold increase, respectively (Figure 6d,e,f).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: At the EMX1 locus in HEK293T cells, the RNPD system represents a 10-fold increase compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system.
source: Compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system this represents a 20-fold, a 10-fold, and a 24-fold increase, respectively (Figure 6d,e,f).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: At the CXCR4 locus in HEK293T cells, the RNPD system represents a 24-fold increase compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system.
source: Compared to the classical CRISPR-Cas9 system this represents a 20-fold, a 10-fold, and a 24-fold increase, respectively (Figure 6d,e,f).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: Direct delivery of Cas9 RNP complexes into tissues promises great potential for therapeutic applications.
source: Direct delivery of Cas9 RNP complexes into tissues promises great potential for therapeutic applications.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of RNP delivery based on established knowledge.

claim: Compared to genetically encoded systems, RNPs avoid the danger of genomic integration.
source: Compared to genetically encoded systems, RNPs avoid the danger of genomic integration
evidence: This is established knowledge about advantages of RNP delivery.

claim: Due to their limited lifetime, RNPs have a low risk of off-target activities.
source: and due to their limited lifetime, the risk of off-target activities is low (Kim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RNP properties, supported by citation.

claim: Procedures for large-scale production of recombinant proteins for clinical use are well established.
source: In addition, procedures for large-scale production of recombinant proteins for clinical use are well established
evidence: This is established knowledge about protein production.

claim: Several recently developed protocols enable in vivo delivery of Cas9 RNP complexes in animal models.
source: and several recently developed protocols enable in vivo delivery of Cas9 RNP complexes in animal models (Wang et al., 2016; Zuris et al., 2015; Staahl et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about recent developments, supported by citations.

claim: The increase in HDR efficiency is caused by enhanced nuclear concentration of the repair template.
source: Our data suggests that the increase in HDR efficiency is caused by enhanced nuclear concentration of the repair template.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Unlike previous approaches that increase HDR rates by chemically modulating DNA repair pathways, the RNPD approach does not alter endogenous cellular processes.
source: Unlike previous approaches that increase HDR rates by chemically modulating DNA repair pathways, our approach does not alter endogenous cellular processes, thus reducing risk of potential negative side effects.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the advantages of the approach.

claim: Covalent linkage of the repair template to the Cas9 RNP complex addresses the challenge that simultaneous delivery of the RNP complex and the repair template needs to be ensured.
source: In addition, covalent linkage of the repair template to the Cas9 RNP complex also addresses another central challenge of in vivo gene editing therapies – namely that simultaneous delivery of the RNP complex and the repair template needs to be ensured.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the approach based on inference.

claim: Covalently linking the DNA repair template to the Cas9 RNP complex is poised to further drive the CRISPR/Cas technology towards clinical translation.
source: Taken together, we suggest that covalently linking the DNA repair template to the Cas9 RNP complex is poised to further drive the CRISPR/Cas technology towards clinical translation.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about the potential impact of the approach.

claim: O6-benzylguanine (BG)-labeled DNA oligos are covalently linked to Cas9-SNAP fusion proteins.
source: O6-benzylguanine (BG)-labeled DNA oligos are covalently linked to Cas9-SNAP fusion proteins.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1 and described in the text.

claim: The DNA-Cas9 molecules are complexed with specific sgRNAs to form functional ribonucleoprotein-DNA (RNPD) complexes.
source: The DNA-Cas9 molecules are then complexed with the specific sgRNAs to form the functional ribonucleoprotein-DNA (RNPD) complexes.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1 and described in the text.

claim: The RFP fluorophore carries a c.190_191delinsCT mutation that substitutes two nucleotides TA at positions 190 and 191 in the RFP sequence to CT.
source: The RFP fluorophore carries a c.190_191delinsCT mutation that substitutes two nucleotides TA at the positions 190 and 191 in the RFP sequence to CT.
evidence: This is described in Figure 2a caption.

claim: The c.190_191delinsCT mutation leads to the inactivation of the RFP fluorophore by the substitution of tyrosine at position 63 with leucine (p.Y63L).
source: This leads to the inactivation the RFP fluorophore by the substitution of tyrosine at the position 63 with leucine (p.Y63L).
evidence: This is described in Figure 2a caption.

claim: Repair of the mutation via donor oligos generates RFP/GFP double positive cells.
source: Repair of the mutation via donor oligos generates RFP/GFP double positive cells
evidence: This is described in Figure 2a caption.

claim: Indel mutations generate RFP/GFP double negative cells if they induce a frame shift.
source: indel mutations generate RFP/GFP double negative cells if they induce a frame shift.
evidence: This is described in Figure 2a caption.

claim: Analysis of the reporter locus by next generation sequencing (NGS) demonstrated that 20 percent of indels did not lead to a frame shift.
source: Of note, analysis of the reporter locus by next generation sequencing (NGS) demonstrated that 20 percent of indels did not lead to a frame shift (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2a caption with reference to supplementary data.

claim: FACS analysis underestimates the absolute number of edited cells.
source: Nevertheless, although FACS analysis thereby underestimates the absolute number of edited cells, it allows to accurately compare the correction efficiencies of different Cas9 systems.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that 20% of indels don't cause frameshift.

claim: FACS analysis allows accurate comparison of the correction efficiencies of different Cas9 systems.
source: Nevertheless, although FACS analysis thereby underestimates the absolute number of edited cells, it allows to accurately compare the correction efficiencies of different Cas9 systems.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 2a caption.
